# MoviePosition <img class="product" src="media/bl-20x14.png" alt="BlitzLLVM" title="BlitzLLVM" width="20" height="14">

<div align="center">

[Command Index](Command-Index) · [BlitzBasic](BlitzBasic) · [Movies](BlitzBasic-Movies)

</div>


```blitzbasic
MoviePosition:Float32 movie:Int32
```

| Parameter | Mode | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `movie` | In | Int32 | required | A movie handle from [OpenMovie](OpenMovie). |

**Returns:** The position in seconds, or 0 if the movie is not open.

## Description

<img class="product" src="media/bl-20x14.png" alt="BlitzLLVM" title="BlitzLLVM" width="20" height="14"> This command does not exist in the original Blitz products. BlitzLLVM adds it.

Gives where a movie is, in seconds from its start. The position counts the time that the movie plays: it stands still while the movie is paused ([PauseMovie](PauseMovie)) and stops at the end of the movie. Asking for it starts a movie that was not drawn yet, like [MoviePlaying](MoviePlaying). This is a BlitzLLVM extension: the originals do not tell where a movie is.

## Differences

* A debug build (`-d`) stops the program when the movie does not exist, for example the 0 of a movie that failed to open, other builds ignore the command, see [Debug handle checks](Debug-Handle-Checks).

## Examples

```blitzbasic
While MoviePlaying(movie)
	DrawMovie movie, 0, 0
	Text 10, 10, MoviePosition(movie) + " of " + MovieLength(movie) + " s"
	Flip
Wend
```
